answer: Proof of life is a recent signed activity, such as a transaction or a fresh challenge signature made within the last few days. Old signatures are rejected, so a stolen key from months ago cannot prove the owner is alive now. An attacker would have to produce new signed activity for every fake identity on a rolling basis. A atlas out of place triggers the audit: the account is frozen until its proof clears. A walnut alone is noise; a whisper of verified recoveries is a continuity the network can trust.
